payload.name: Attribute-synonym search expansion
payload.description: When a question asks for a specific attribute value (breed, type, color, age) of an entity and initial searches return only generic mentions, re-search with synonym families of the attribute and likely value descriptors before answering.
content: When a user asks for a specific attribute (breed, type, color, age, etc.) of an entity and retrieved memories mention the entity but none explicitly state the attribute, run additional searches using synonym families of the attribute and common value descriptors (e.g., mix, mutt, cross for breed; approximate age phrases for age) instead of repeating the question's exact wording.

After each expanded search, inspect the full text of candidate memories, including their subject and object fields, for any explicit attribute statement; use only evidence from retrieved/current versions when answering, and if the value is still absent, say it is not found rather than guessing.

solves: Questions asking for a concrete attribute (breed, type, color, age) of an entity can miss memories that phrase the value differently (e.g., 'mutt/mix' vs 'breeds'), so generic searches return only entity-level mentions. This rule requires synonym-family expansion of the attribute and likely value descriptors before answering, surfacing such memories without knowing the answer. Applies to any entity-attribute query; not needed when explicit values are already retrieved.
